test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A and B are emptying pipes and C is a filling pipe. Pipes A and B can empty a full tank in 15 hours and 18 hours, respectively. When all three pipes are opened together, it takes 1(1)/(4) hours to empty (1)/(9) part of the tank. In how many hours can pipe C alone fill (2)/(3) part of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net emptying part in 1 hour by (A + B + C) = (1/9) ÷ (5/4) = 4/45 part/hour.

Part emptied by A and B in 1 hour = 1/15 + 1/18 = 11/90 part/hour.

Filling part by C in 1 hour = (Part emptied by A + B) − Net emptying part.

Efficiency of C = 11/90 − 4/45 = 11/90 − 8/90 = 3/90 = 1/30 part/hour.

Time required for C to fill 2/3 part = (2/3) ÷ (1/30) = 20 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to empty the tank = 15 hours

Time taken by B to empty the tank = 18 hours

Time taken by A, B, and C to empty 1/9 part of the tank = 5/4 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by A, B, and C together to empty the full tank = (5/4) × 9 = 45/4 hours

⇒ Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of (15, 18, and 45) = 90 units.

⇒ Note: Emptying efficiencies are taken as negative.

⇒ Efficiency of A + B + C = −8

⇒ (−6) + (−5) + Efficiency of C = −8

⇒ −11 + Efficiency of C = −8

⇒ Efficiency of C = −8 + 11 = +3 units/hour (Positive sign indicates filling pipe)

⇒ We need to find the time taken by C to fill 2/3 part of the tank.

⇒ Required capacity to fill = 2/3 × 90 = 60 units

⇒ Time taken by pipe C = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another can empty it in y hours, their combined filling rate is (1/x − 1/y) per hour.

Negative Efficiency

Emptying pipes are assigned a negative efficiency since they constantly act against the total capacity to be filled.

LCM Method

Taking the LCM of the individual times provides a convenient unit value for the total capacity of the tank, thereby avoiding fractional calculations.
